pr_body:
Close #195 #197 #356

This PR replaces PR #321 

Also, revert an early all-reduce optimization that stores all all-reduce results in a shared buffer. This can lead to wrong results in distributed settings for models with two parallel all-reduce branches.

Correctness check:
- [x] tiiuae/falcon-rw-1b
- [x] tiiuae/falcon-rw-7b
- [x] tiiuae/falcon-7b
- [x] tiiuae/falcon-7b-instruct
- [x] tiiuae/falcon-40b
- [x] tiiuae/falcon-40b-instruct

issue_context.title: Support for Falcon-7B / 40B models
issue_context.body: It would be great, if you can add support for Falcon models as well!  Does it support onnx models today?
comments: Currently, vLLM does not support ONNX models. Supporting Falcon is on our roadmap. Thanks for your suggestion.
@WoosukKwon When do you anticipate adding support for Falcon to vLLM?
@MotzWanted I'm working on it now. I think we can add less-optimized version of Falcon (MQA replaced by MHA) quickly (within a few days) and then develop kernels to make the model actually use MQA.
I'm waiting for supporting Falcon families, too. Thanks a lot for your works.

review_comments:
Dumb questions:
1. Why is this the only layer that uses Falcon Linear?
2. Can't we simply use the regular Linear layer for this? Does it really affect the model accuracy?

You can see the notes on Falcon Linear above. Normal linear layer fuses matmul and bias-add, which will not be correct for Falcons. All other layers are `ColumnParallelLinear` or `RowParallelLinear` with `skip_bias_add=True`, which is effectively the same as `FalconLinear`.
Could you comment that this is required to support the original falcon models like `tiiuae/falcon-7b` and the falcon models after the new HF release do not use it?
Can you elaborate on (and comment) how this attribute is related to identifying if the model uses MQA?
